title: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: hunt on Microsoft Teams calls and meetings
summary: Hold: Microsoft explicitly includes CallActivityEvents in the ISOC 90-day retention benefit, so its retention eligibility is not an open question. The briefing also promises no change for end users despite correctly saying that Microsoft has not stated the arrival default. The roadmap facts and Plan 2 licensing are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap says security admins with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 can hunt on Teams calls and meetings in their organisation.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Unified RBAC controls users' access to Defender advanced hunting data, including Teams collaboration data.
claims.quote: Unless otherwise stated, all permissions are applicable to all supported workloads and will be applied to the data scope selected during the data source and assignment stage.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/custom-permissions-details for the general reach of unified RBAC. Retain the narrower statement that the overview does not explicitly name CallActivityEvents.

claims.claim: The Defender portal path Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role reaches the role-creation experience.
claims.quote: On the Permissions page, under Microsoft Defender XDR, select Roles > Create custom role.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions'. Add to the note: 'Select the required permissions on Choose permissions; then use Assign users and data sources > Add assignment to select employees and data sources.' These steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/create-custom-rbac-roles. Keep the caveat that the overview does not name CallActivityEvents.
